hero.h1: Tankless Water Heaters in Lincoln Park, Chicago
hero.sub: In a city home where every square foot counts, a wall-mounted tankless heater frees up space and never runs out mid-shower. We install, repair and descale them, and we tell you honestly if one fits your home. Our office is on Diversey Parkway.

img.alt: Plumber working on the copper water lines of a wall-mounted tankless water heater in a basement

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: A tankless heater heats water only when a hot tap opens, so there's no tank to keep hot all day. Water passes through a heat exchanger and comes out hot as long as the tap runs. Each unit has a flow limit, so it's sized for the most hot water you'll use at once.

head: Tank
Tankless

blocks.h2: Is Tankless Right for Your Lincoln Park Home?
blocks.intro: Many homes here are good candidates. A few things need checking.

items.body: Gas tankless units usually vent through an outside wall, which isn't always easy in attached buildings.
Gas units need a larger supply than a tank. Electric units need a lot of power.
Some associations have rules about exterior vents.
A wall unit frees up a closet or basement corner.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: We check the building before recommending a unit.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: A tankless heater can open up a whole closet in a condo unit, but a gas unit usually needs a vent through an outside wall, and any unit needs enough gas or electric capacity. In many Lincoln Park buildings, exterior vents need board approval, and some units don't have a wall that reaches outside. We'll look at your unit and building first and tell you honestly whether tankless is practical.

blocks.h2: Tankless Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Can I put a tankless heater in my condo?
items.answer: Often. The unit needs a vent through an exterior wall and an adequate gas or electric supply. Check your association's rules too.

items.q: How often does a tankless heater need descaling?
items.answer: About once a year for most homes.
Yes. We diagnose error codes, descale and replace failed parts.

items.q: Will my gas line need an upgrade?
items.answer: Often. Gas tankless units need more gas at once than a tank. We check before we quote.

items.q: Are electric tankless heaters an option?
items.answer: For some units, if the electrical service is large enough. Many need an upgrade.

items.q: How much does a tankless water heater cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the unit and venting. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the unit, venting and supply work. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
